newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-HINGIS COASTS INTO SECOND ROUND IN CHICAGO.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-HINGIS COASTS INTO SECOND ROUND IN CHICAGO.

text.p: Swiss teen sensation Martina Hingis turned her first-round match into a light workout at the Ameritech Cup tennis tournament on Monday.
The fifth-seeded Hingis took just 40 minutes to steamroll American Jolene Watanabe 6-1 6-1 in a match the precocious 16-year-old said was "like practice for me."
"I have more confidence in what I'm doing," said Hingis, who is coming off her first tour victory at Filderstadt, Germany.
"Two years ago, I wouldn't have played her like I did today. I feel very prepared coming in to this tournament."
Hingis, whose ranking is up to a career-high eighth in the world, will get her chance to show just how prepared she is later in the week.
Six of the top 10 players in the world are entered here, including co-world number one Monica Seles, who will play her first match in more than a month on Wednesday.

Seles has not played competitively since leading the United States to the Fed Cup title over Spain last month. She spent the last four weeks undergoing a training regimen aimed and avoiding surgery on her injured shoulder.
Hingis easily and efficiently covered the entire court Monday in beating Watanabe for the third time in as many meetings.
In the second set Hingis gave up just four points against her serve -- one in each game -- and clinched victory with an ace.
"Her serve was much better than the last time I played her," said the 95th-ranked Watanabe, who lost to Hingis in Berlin in May and at the Australian Open in 1995.
Watanabe said she was surprised by Hingis's aggressive tactics.
"She came in a lot and caught me off guard, actually," Watanabe said. "From the first time I played her to now is a big improvement. Her shot is much crisper."
